wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says mines hit seven tankers in Hormuz overnight and 2 supertankers after, and its strait authority has blacklisted 122 ships. Lavrov and Munir carried mediation to Tehran, which says no enriched uranium will leave, and the US pulled nonessential staff from Saudi Arabia.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says seven tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, then claimed two more supertankers struck its mines, and a Houthi drone strike on Shaybah sent Brent to $110.63. The rally is in paper: futures rose $10 in two weeks while physical barrels sank.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The Gulf war set the price: Iran's Guards said mines set 2 tankers ablaze in Hormuz, and shipping US crude to Asia now costs $40 a barrel, Vitol says. Trump's easing of sanctions on Russian fuel took some heat out, while Ukrainian drones hit an oil terminal in St Petersburg. US gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in September.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: With Hormuz closed, Dutch benchmark gas climbed above $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres and Qatar agreed to import up to 4 million tons of US gas yearly. None of that overseas demand for American supply accounts for the slide in the US price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Egypt offered mills wheat from LE16,500 a tonne to hold down unsubsidized bread prices, and Pakistan set its 2027 crop price at Rs4,500 per maund, Rs1,000 above last year. Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships in the Black Sea, where the attacks threaten grain supplies.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Mined ore has grown so scarce that the fees Chinese smelters charge to process it have collapsed, and they plan more output cuts before annual talks with miners. Supply stayed tight elsewhere: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine for over a week, and Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper, a trader turning lender to secure metal.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Oil drove the climb: Brent at $103.70 on the Gulf war pushed bets on a Fed holding rates higher for longer, and the IMF warned of a global debt squeeze. The retreat came with AI doubts, as a chip rout sank the Kospi more than 7% and money moved into the yen and US bonds, while Warsh withheld guidance.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fortnight's stories about American stocks concerned future supply rather than price: Goldman expects $1.7 trillion in 2027 unlocks, matched by buybacks, and Broadcom, Verizon and other issuers refused tokenization. None of it accounts for the index's path.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The fortnight's news about its biggest members was mostly Meta's: a $25 billion judgment in New Mexico, free cash flow turning negative, and new nonvoting shares that Wall Street wants gone. Apple's iPhone Duo was backordered until 2027. None of it explains the index's own moves.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Pump prices follow crude, and the Gulf war has held oil near $105 a barrel. Fuel is tight enough that Trump eased sanctions on Russian fuel: the first 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel left Primorsk for New York, with Rosneft, itself sanctioned, supplying most of the deal.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar is routing gas around Hormuz: a tanker bound for Poland is crossing the Red Sea, and Doha signed to import up to 4 million tons of US gas a year through 2054. Dutch benchmark futures hit about $1,003 per 1,000 cubic metres in October, and gas explains £161 of a £180 rise in UK bills.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's news was dominated by France's school protests turning into a political crisis and by Rubio's talks in Mumbai amid a crude oil crisis, and none of it accounts for the index's path.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Islamabad set farmers a wheat price of Rs4,500 per 40kg maund, cut petrol while nudging diesel up in its fortnightly review, and completed ratification of the Makkah defence pact with Saudi Arabia. None of it explains the exchange rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigerian inflation has fallen to about 15% from about 35%, and the central bank restated its inflation target, but food inflation rose to 19.59% as the headline rate fell. None of that accounts for a rate that barely moved over the fortnight.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Moody's upgrade, which left Egypt 6 notches below investment grade, usually supports a currency, and the same week Egypt's council approved troops for Saudi Arabia's war with the Houthis. Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the pound's weakening.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's news about Turkey was diplomatic and military: Ankara sent the Makkah defence pact binding it to defend Riyadh to parliament, Istanbul hosted Iran war mediators, and four states demanded Hormuz reopen. A gas platform set to double Sakarya field output also launched. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's stories touched the migrant labour whose remittances prop up the currency, with Malaysia-bound Bangladeshis paying up to 400,000 taka in recruitment costs and Saudi Arabia executing two Bangladeshis without telling Dhaka, but none of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: MSCI moved to cut Indonesia's status and drop it from its global indexes, and Jakarta stocks fell to a six-year low. A further 11.6% slide on Friday was the worst day since 1998. Funds that track those indexes sell the shares and take their money out in dollars, which weakens the rupiah.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The news out of Lebanon was the war: Israeli attacks had killed 4,387 people in Lebanon, and fresh strikes hit southern Lebanon days later, deepening a cost of living crisis years in the making. None of it moved the pound.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight's yuan news was about the market's plumbing, not its price: the PBOC said it will lend to funds, not just banks, to backstop the bond market, and Hong Kong's bond clearinghouse, with around 200 members, set out to court more foreign banks for yuan clearing. Neither accounts for the rate's drift.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: Rubio came to Mumbai tying India's waiver on Russian oil to its trade deal, and pressed its refineries to process more Venezuelan crude; India's 17th free trade agreement, with New Zealand, took effect the same week. None of it was reported as the reason the rupee firmed.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The fortnight in Brazil was dominated by the Lula–Flávio Bolsonaro runoff, with polls showing it tied, and by official data showing prices up 4.62% in a year, through the upper limit of the central bank's target. None of it accounts for the real's strength.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Mexico's own news over the fortnight was about prices and corporate exits. Inflation reached 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, and AT&T sold its 24.7 million Mexican subscribers to Televisa for $2 billion. Neither accounts for a move of this size in the currency.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: European gas futures topped $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres with storage at a record low, the Iran war's energy shock landing on a bloc that imports its fuel. France added strain: school protests became a political crisis and its 10-year yield hit the highest since 2002. Lagarde has since pointed the ECB toward a December hike.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen firmed when doubts about AI sent money into it as a refuge. It started from a weakness Japan feels at the till: yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and Tokyo is debating wage-driven inflation with the Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate already a 31-year high.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble firmed as Russia's oil earnings rose: the Hormuz crisis kept Brent above $109, Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he signed into law, and the first 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel left for New York under his deal with Putin. Russia then kept its key rate at 14%, holding up the returns that draw money into rubles.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The month's South African news was domestic: a budget that cuts the fuel levy until January 2027, a judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, and Merz urging Trump to invite South Africa to the G-20 summit in Miami. None of it accounts for the rand's path.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Two threads ran against it. MSCI drew up rules that would eject bitcoin treasury firms from its indices, and JPMorgan estimated $2.8 billion in outflows from Strategy stock alone. Google's Willow chip revived the quantum threat to the 6.4 million bitcoin whose public keys are already exposed, and Coinbase urged a quantum-resistant fix now.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Late in the window, crypto traders moved out of altcoins and into bitcoin as ETF flows wobbled. DeFi tokens, which mostly run on Ethereum, led the market lower after bitcoin gave up Wednesday's surge, so ether fell with the tokens built on it.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Gold fell 3.6% this week, its worst since June. The Gulf war has lifted oil, oil feeds inflation, and that pushes the Fed toward holding rates higher for longer, which raises the cost of owning a metal that pays nothing. Official demand held beneath the slide: China's central bank bought 23 tonnes in September.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Nothing reported on the peak day accounts for it. The days after brought a Beijing draft export list covering 23 AI technologies, including model weights; Warsh calling AI a shock to the economy; and Barclays cutting 5% of staff while paying shareholders £500 million.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Washington and Moscow moved toward a deal: Trump put on hold sanctions he had signed into law, the first 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel left Primorsk for New York, and Putin freed Stephen Hubbard during Steve Witkoff's visit. The Kremlin confirmed November talks with Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, while a drone sank a cargo ship off Constanța.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said mines struck 7 tankers overnight, then two supertankers carrying 4.5 million barrels, as Tehran offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days if the US accepted its conditions. Lavrov came to mediate, and Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey jointly demanded the strait reopen, TASS reported.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran is using mines to decide which ships may pass. The IRGC says seven tankers were hit on 22 October and two more supertankers since, claims carried by TASS and Mehr. Qatar has sent a gas tanker toward Poland via the Red Sea, and Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey jointly demanded the strait reopen.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Fighting reached the strait's Yemen shore: the government says it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, and military sources counted 63 dead in 24 hours. Ships kept passing anyway. A Qatari gas tanker is crossing the Red Sea toward Poland, and China and Djibouti jointly backed free navigation through it.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Gulf cargo is taking the canal route: a Qatari gas tanker is crossing the Red Sea toward Poland while the Iran war goes on. The southern approach stays contested. Egypt pledged support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks, and China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The strait's oil traffic starts at Hormuz, where mines set tankers ablaze this week. Vitol said shipping US crude to Asia now costs $40 a barrel, and Asian refiners are turning to smaller tankers. None of this reported a change in transits through Malacca itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news touched shipping in the strait. The Taiwan story was diplomatic: Beijing sanctioned Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over their countries' ties to Taiwan, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The past fortnight's news carried El Niño setting an all-time Pacific temperature record and a UN call to arms against it, but nothing about the canal's water levels, its draft limits or its traffic, and none of it accounts for the transits.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones have been striking merchant ships in the Black Sea: one sank off Bulgaria with 11 sailors missing, and the attacks entered a NATO country's territorial waters for the first time. Germany warned the strikes threaten grain supplies, NATO reinforced its patrols, and a drone then sank the Khoryv off Constanța, which Romania blamed on Russia.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news that reaches this strait was about Russian oil. Washington temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel and weighed easing them on shadow fleet tankers, the sanctioned trade that sails past Gibraltar, and Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy. None of it accounts for the vessel count.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: France's fortnight was riots, curfews and a 200,000-tonne monthly Gulf diesel deal, and none of it reached shipping through the Dover Strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news centred on Hormuz, where the Revolutionary Guards said mines set tankers ablaze, and on freight: Vitol says shipping US crude to Asia now costs $40 a barrel. None of it accounts for traffic past the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's Black Sea shipping news came from the western shore. Drones sank cargo ships off Krapets in Bulgaria and off Constanța in Romania, and NATO sent patrol planes and drones after at least 23 sailors were left missing or dead. None of it reported anything at the strait itself.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news from Türkiye was diplomatic and military: the Makkah defence pact sent to parliament, a Canada partnership, a gas platform at Filyos, the government's takeover of an independent TV channel, and Ankara warning against a renewed attack on Iran. None of it accounts for the slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Malaysia was about a ban on civil servants using Waze, six young people suing the government over deforestation, and a Tanaka plant to recover gold from chip-factory scrap. None of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: After months of warnings, MSCI moved to cut Indonesia's status and remove it from its global indexes, which forces funds that track those benchmarks to sell. Jakarta stocks plunged 10% to a six-year low on the news, then fell 11.6% in a single session, the worst day since 1998.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Doubts over AI spending hit Asian chip stocks in mid-October, with Samsung and SK Hynix dragging Seoul's index down 5.5%, and the same jitters sent money into the yen, which reached a one-month high of 156.28 per dollar. A stronger yen cuts what exporters earn abroad, while import costs up 24.5% kept a Bank of Japan rate hike in view.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Hong Kong's own news was about the market's plumbing: the regulator froze HK$4.38 billion over suspected faked public-offering demand, and Valcambi agreed to refine gold in the city. Mainland new-energy car sales fell 17% and the EU planned to halve imports of Chinese hybrids, but nothing reported ties any of it to the index's slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The economic news was strong: exports up 36% in September, and growth and retail sales above forecast. None of it explains the slide. The signs of strain sat elsewhere. The central bank will now lend to funds, not just banks, to steady bonds, and robot shares valued at 22 billion yuan drew no bids at 12 billion.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the index down 5.5% on doubts over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and a chip rout two days later took more than 7% off it. The doubt spread to new listings: Elice closed 30% below its offer price, and SK hynix shelved a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight brought Jio Platforms' record offering of up to ₹30,213 crore, Fairfax buying 60.72% of IDBI Bank, September food inflation of 7.74%, and Rubio tying India's Russian oil waiver to its trade deal. None of these stories is reported as the cause of the index's slide.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's news over the period was about other things: the worst haze since 2015 from Indonesian fires, freight for US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel by Vitol's count, and a yen lifted by AI doubts. None of it concerns the banks and property firms the index is built on, or explains its slide.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The pullback followed the chip trade across Asia: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged Seoul's benchmark down 5.5% on doubts over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and TSMC's shares fell even after a record profit for the sixth straight quarter. In Taoyuan, one of Micron's two Taiwan unions struck over bonuses.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's fortnight brought a mid-term budget that cut the fuel levy until January 2027 and a Pretoria judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, but neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: The fortnight's news was the runoff: polls put Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly ahead of Lula, business elites who once scorned him rushed to meet him, and inflation broke through the central bank's target ceiling at 4.62%. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news out of Mexico accounts for the climb. AT&T agreed to sell its 24.7 million Mexican subscribers for $2 billion, and inflation reached 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, but neither moves an index of this breadth on its own.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina posted a second straight month of inflation below 2%, and lodged a legal claim against the UK's Falklands oil exploration, but nothing in the input explains why the index fell.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight's Canadian news was Alberta voting 76% to stay in Canada, inflation reaching 3.1% on gasoline up 27.8% in a year, and Fairfax winning IDBI Bank in India. None of it is tied to the index's moves.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Several of the index's biggest names reported weak third-quarter numbers. Tesla's net profit fell 43% to $787 million, Meta's free cash flow turned negative the day after a New Mexico case cost it $25 billion, and Comcast lost 144,000 US broadband customers and called its rivals irrational.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The UK business news of the fortnight was Barclays cutting 5% of its staff while paying shareholders £500 million, and gas driving most of a £180 rise in UK electricity bills ahead of a costly winter. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Germany's business news over the fortnight was about single firms: Volkswagen planned a pay freeze for 660,000 workers until 2030, and Amazon pledged €16 billion for data centers. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's 10-year bond yield reached 4.96%, its highest since 2002, as riots with nearly 2,400 arrests in one night grew into a political crisis and the European Central Bank headed for a December hike. Dearer state borrowing raises what French companies pay too, though nothing reported ties the index's slide to one event.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML, the index's heaviest stock, reported that China's share of its sales jumped from 14% to 23%, a 109% rise in equipment sales there despite a US push for export curbs. Demand runs far ahead of supply: customers are already asking ASML for lithography tools in 2029 and 2030.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight brought floods that killed four in the east, Milei rallying the far right to oust Sanchez, and the opposition backing De Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: As the slide reached its trough, the ECB's Panetta said rising bond yields will restrain the economy. That is the channel this index is built on: costlier sovereign debt weighs on the Italian banks that hold it. Earlier in the month, Unipol won ECB and Bank of Italy approval for de facto control of BPER Banca.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The fortnight's news from Stockholm was an economics Nobel for modelling economic shocks and Sweden's central bank reviving its e-krona debate, and neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The run-up to Israel's election brought Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu, an unannounced visit from Hegseth and a doctrine making preemptive war official policy, then a Hebron cordon after 5 Israelis were wounded. None of the reporting ties any of it to share prices.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump's diesel deal with Russia opened a rift with Europe, and Germany and Ukraine pressed for Putin to join a full energy-sector truce. Talks in Oslo followed, Witkoff went on to Moscow, and Putin proposed a three-way summit with no Ukrainian seat. At home, Zacharia was ousted after 5 days as White House Press Secretary.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Gasoline lifted September's US inflation to 3.7% over the year, turning bets toward a hike. In Bangkok, Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance, while Gulf war oil prices strengthened the case for keeping rates higher for longer. Trump also opened a probe into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank is heading for a December hike. Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation over the next year, up from 3%, as the Iran war's energy shock reaches what they expect to pay. Lagarde has pointed to a bond selloff in which France's growing debt woes pushed up borrowing costs.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's reporting on precious metals was about gold, not silver: conflicting Iran signals clouding the path for rates, a digital gold market tripling as younger investors piled in, and mining felling forests from Ghana to the Amazon. None of it accounts for silver's price.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove September's reading: prices rose 0.6% in that month alone, more than expected. The figure landed weeks before the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell the next day on fears of tighter policy.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran now decides which ships pass: its strait authority has blacklisted 122 vessels, and the Revolutionary Guard says its mines hit seven tankers on 22 October and two supertankers since. Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey demanded the strait reopen. Shipping US crude to Asia instead costs $40 a barrel, Vitol says.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthis' war with Saudi Arabia struck airports in Riyadh and Dammam and the oil route through Yanbu, not ships in the strait. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, and a Qatari gas tanker crossed it toward Poland; none of it accounts for the container traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The Houthi strikes of the fortnight landed on Saudi Arabia's airports in Riyadh and Dammam and on the Shaybah oilfield, not on shipping, and nothing reported from the war accounts for the canal's traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The news since the chart ends is about Hormuz, not here: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says its mines have hit tankers there, and Vitol puts the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel. Gulf crude bound for Asia passes through Malacca, but nothing in the input explains this count.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: A Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people and emptied the capital's skies, and Qatar Airways suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam. Missiles then set an Aramco building in Dhahran on fire and hit near the presidential palace in Aden. The US ordered families out of Saudi Arabia, and the investor summit was postponed to 2027.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: US inflation rose before the midterm elections, fuelling rate hike fears, a day after the IMF warned the UK of inflation risk ahead of its first budget. The oil shock from the war then spread: gasoline in Canada cost 27.8% more than a year earlier, and Brazil's inflation broke through its target ceiling days before the runoff.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Germany and Ukraine pressed Putin to join a full energy-sector truce, while Trump's diesel deal with Russia opened a rift with Europe. Days later Ukraine's drones set a St Petersburg oil terminal burning, Russia hit 28 energy facilities and 550,000 households lost power, and the Kremlin confirmed talks in Abu Dhabi in November.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The only related story in the fortnight was the FBI naming SafePay among the most active ransomware gangs, with more than 600 victims since 2024. Nothing in it accounts for the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The White House said there would be no strike before the 3 November midterms, and the strikes Trump is reported to be weighing fall in the days after them, past this contract's end date. Mediation also kept moving: Lavrov offered it in Tehran, Munir carried proposals there, and seven foreign ministers met in Istanbul.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its blockade of Iran before a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, and it moves with every sign of a deal or of escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Mediation stalled: Lavrov and Munir carried proposals to Tehran, and Iran's security chief answered that no enriched uranium will leave. Meanwhile the Revolutionary Guard claimed mine hits on tankers in Hormuz, Iran's strait authority blacklisted 122 ships, and Washington pulled nonessential staff from Saudi Arabia.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between Israel and Iran is still in force on October 31. Its price is what traders will stake on the truce surviving, and it moves on strikes, talks and threats from either side.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The pressure came from the Gulf rather than from Israel itself: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said 7 tankers were hit in Hormuz, then 2 supertankers carrying 4.5 million barrels struck mines, and the US pulled nonessential staff from Saudi Arabia. Mediation ran alongside, with Munir carrying proposals to Tehran and seven foreign ministers called to Istanbul.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Rivals pressed on two fronts. In China, Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months and took share from Nvidia there. In Redmond, Microsoft said it will deploy its own Maia chips across Azure by the gigawatt.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened on 16 October, and the phone was soon backordered until 2027, three days after Apple unveiled HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home. The same week Apple Intelligence entered China, running on Alibaba's Qwen models, which gave the phone's AI features a route into that market.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google halved the price of Gemini 4 Argon, its only UK cloud region failed and hit Revolut, banks and courts, and a new privacy policy lets Gmail data feed ad targeting once users turn on Personal Intelligence. None of the reporting ties any of these to the share price.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: The fortnight brought a report that Amazon may spend $7 billion on Decart, an AI startup Anthropic walked away from after offering $6 billion, and the launch of AI devices that hear conversations. Neither accounts for the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: TSMC reported record profit for the sixth straight quarter in mid-October, and the shares fell after the results rather than rising. Nothing in the input explains why a record result was sold.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: The peak came as Microsoft announced a multi-gigawatt rollout of its own Maia AI chips across Azure. Six days later it dropped a planned AI data-centre site with Nscale in Loughton, where grid power may wait a decade. Norway fined its Xandr unit a record €8.5 million over Grindr user data.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: Broadcom joined Verizon and 7 other issuers in refusing to let the SEC's tokenized stock framework turn their shares into tokens, a dispute over how the stock trades rather than over the business, and nothing in the input accounts for the fall in the share.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: Last quarter SpaceX spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure. Ukraine accused it of throttling Starlink terminals, cutting drone links at 110 km/h, and Ukrainian sources saw no change after Trump said Musk had restored access. None of it, nor Musk's pledge of SpaceX shares to children, accounts for the share's path.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta lost a New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica in which 43 million deception violations cost it $25 billion. The next day it reported free cash flow of negative $2.12 billion, and created nonvoting shares that Zuckerberg can partly sell freely, an overhang Wall Street wants gone.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: A missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran after the Saudi-led coalition hit a Houthi site. Four days later the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, a warning carried by Iran's state agency Mehr. A Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field followed.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla reported a 43% fall in third-quarter net profit, to $787 million, on the same day word came that it and SpaceX were exploring a merger, a combination that would hold 30,000 BTC. Five days earlier it unveiled the 2026 Roadster, priced at $200,000 or more, which Munster called an engineering flex with a SpaceX clue.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: On 2026-10-13 Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% in one session. The sell-off came from doubts over AI spending and from the threat of Chinese memory rivals, and it hit the two firms that dominate the market hardest.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan went on strike on Thursday in Taoyuan as a dispute over bonuses escalated. Nothing reported so far ties the stoppage to output or connects it to the share's retreat from its peak.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: Lilly began trials of a cousin of its obesity drug against alcohol use disorder. Walmart said it would pay for some GLP-1s at no cost to its workers, and Belgium refused to reimburse Mounjaro. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK hynix shelved a listing worth up to $15 billion for Solidigm, its US NAND flash arm bought from Intel, keeping it in-house as AI data centres drive flash demand; investors rewarded the call. Ten days earlier, fears over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals had sent it and Samsung down hard enough to drag South Korea's benchmark 5.5% lower.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one company news in the window was about its workforce, not its trading: Walmart said it would offer employees 250-plus medications at no cost, including GLP-1s and insulin. A benefits change of that kind does not account for the share's climb.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Customers are already asking ASML for lithography tools to be delivered in 2029 and 2030. China's share of its sales jumped from 14% to 23%, with equipment sales there up 109% despite the US push for export curbs. Neither explains the latest fall in the share.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated on Oct 15 as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. Forced selling of that kind falls on the large tokens together. Solana's own news was technical: it set Oct 21 for Alpenglow, an upgrade targeting 150-millisecond finality.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: It fell with the altcoin sell-off: nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid, and traders sought shelter in bitcoin. A fix for the bug that threatened the 100 billion XRP cap slipped to November after validator support dipped, and Franklin Templeton's $150 million fund arrived on the ledger freezable by its issuer.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The one prominent story about the exchange in the fortnight was Jeff Yan's plan to bring the entire financial industry onto Hyperliquid, and nothing in it accounts for the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Leveraged crypto traders were flushed out in mid-October, when nearly $1 billion in bets was liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. A week later ZEC jumped 11% as AI earnings revived tech and bitcoin hovered around $83,000.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: No Bank of England decision fell in the fortnight. The argument was over whether to move at all: officials divided over the inflation risk facing the UK, and Greene said those risks were bigger than thought, as gas drove £161 of a £180 rise in UK bills.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and Ueda said the BOJ can't tolerate underlying inflation running further over 2%. Finance minister Katayama described Japan as shifting to wage-driven inflation, and the IMF said the BOJ may need to tighten faster if prices beat its forecast.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The central bank acted around the rate rather than through it this fortnight. It said it will lend to funds, not just banks, to backstop the bond market, and it bought 23 tonnes of gold in September as it moves reserves away from the dollar. Neither step touches the rate's level.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia kept its key rate on hold on Friday and named high inflation expectations as a point of concern. It credited rising export revenues for the ruble's strength, and the ruble's climb slowed after the decision. The bank also kept buying yuan through the month.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The IMF and World Bank held their meetings in Bangkok this month, dominated by the Hormuz closure, poor-country debt and AI, but none of it concerned Thailand's own companies or economy, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles and drones reached Saudi soil: a strike shut Riyadh's airport, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell. Saudi Arabia postponed its investor summit to 2027, the US ordered diplomats' families out, and a drone attack on Dammam airport killed two.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The Iran war's grip on Hormuz ran through the fortnight: Iran said Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening the strait, six ships were hit there in one day, and the UAE reported non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter. In Dubai, fuel costs rose 37.52% in a year.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: September inflation hit 7.2% against a 2-4% target, and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas answered with a 50 basis point hike to 5.50% to defend a weakening peso. An oil importer, the Philippines pays more as oil tops $110 after a Houthi drone strike near Saudi Shaybah field, so its firms face dearer fuel and dearer credit at once.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta lost a New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica, where 43 million deception violations cost it $25 billion. The next day it reported free cash flow of negative $2.12 billion. It also created nonvoting shares, 20% of which Zuckerberg can sell freely, an overhang Wall Street wants gone.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: The peak came the day Microsoft announced a multi-gigawatt rollout of its own Maia AI chips in Azure racks. It has since dropped Nscale's planned AI site at Loughton, where grid power may wait a decade, and Norway fined its Xandr ad unit a record €8.5 million over Grindr user data.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Fed Chair Warsh spoke in Bangkok of AI as a shock to the economy and withheld guidance on this meeting. Since then the Gulf war's oil prices have kept inflation sticky and pushed the Fed toward holding rates higher for longer, and the money has moved onto no change before the decision next week.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent's own news in these weeks was housekeeping in AI agents: it is shutting the QClaw desktop agent on 24 December, put the WorkBuddy agent into WeCom's contact list, and offered developers 2,000 free search calls a month. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba's Qwen models went into the China beta of Apple Intelligence, and its N1 Pro glasses launched with iris-scan payment verification, but neither product story accounts for the fall in its share.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The fortnight's news about Amazon itself was all expansion. It pledged €16 billion in Germany for data centers and Prime as the shares reached their high. It also launched AI devices that hear conversations, and it was reported ready to spend $7 billion on Decart, the AI startup Anthropic walked away from after offering $6 billion.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: Researchers logged over 1,000 Meta restrictions on political content. Meta then admitted its AI generated images favouring Flávio Bolsonaro, and Lula's campaign says Meta AI refused his posters but made Flávio's. None of it accounts for the swings in this bet.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX reported its quarterly revenue doubling, and that it spent $16.4 billion of it on AI infrastructure. Ukrainian officials said Starlink cut out on drones above set speeds, which Musk blamed on Washington, and a NASA adviser said Artemis IV needs 22 Starship refuelling flights.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news bears on which party takes the Senate or the House. What it carried about prediction markets was regulatory: 39 states and 145 tribal nations urged Supreme Court review, and a Pentagon memo said insider bets put troops' lives at risk.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The war reached the company's own sites: a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and a Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field pushed Brent above $110. In between, the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, Mehr reported, and the kingdom's output sank to a record 6.24 million barrels daily.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The one story of the fortnight about Nvidia's own business came from China, where its share of the AI chip market fell as Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months. Nothing else in the input concerns the company's sales, orders or rules on where it may sell, and that one report does not by itself account for the slide.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu heads the government formed after Israel's next election. The premiership needs a 61-seat Knesset majority, so coalition arithmetic moves it as much as votes do.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: In the run-up to the election, Trump endorsed Netanyahu and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met him in an unannounced visit. Separately, former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar sued him for 3 million shekels. None of it accounts for the swings in what traders will pay.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable listed company, a Mumbai conglomerate that runs the Jamnagar refining complex alongside Jio telecoms and India's biggest retail chain. Its size makes it a swing stock for the whole Indian market.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Jio Platforms priced India's largest share sale, seeking up to ₹30,213 crore, and drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand that included sovereign funds. Reliance said its satellite service awaits the same clearances as Starlink, and Rubio pressed India's refiners to process Venezuelan crude. None of it explains the share's dip.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in Tesla, the US maker of electric cars and grid batteries, listed on Nasdaq. Its valuation rests more on bets about self-driving cars and robots than on the cars it sells today, so it moves on Elon Musk's promises.
stocks:TSLA.recent: Tesla reported a 43% fall in net profit, to $787 million, as its margins shrank. The same day, it and SpaceX were reported to be exploring a merger. Days earlier the company had unveiled the 2026 Roadster, an EV sports car priced from $200,000.

stocks:HSBA.L.standing: One of Europe's largest banks, headquartered in London but earning most of its profit in Asia, above all in Hong Kong. Its London shares move on Asian interest rates and on the state of relations between China and the West.

stocks:V.standing: The largest card payment network in the world, routing transactions between the banks that issue cards and those that accept them. It earns a fee on each payment and lends nothing, so its revenue tracks consumer spending.
stocks:V.recent: Visa won preliminary approval to clear yuan card payments in China, a step toward handling domestic transactions there rather than only cross-border ones. It also moved further into stablecoins, linking crypto to cash alongside Mastercard and Stripe, while Polygon completed its purchase of Coinme to compete with Visa and Stripe in global payments.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The government's claimed gains came at Dhubab and on the Mocha road near Bab al-Mandeb, far from Sanaa, while the Houthis hit Riyadh's airport and fired missiles at Yanbu. A government claim of 800 Houthi casualties on the eastern front followed, and Houthi missiles then killed 18 recruits at a Shabwa training camp.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman, the two states whose coasts form the Strait of Hormuz, reach an agreement on the strait before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through that channel.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guard turned the strait into a mine field, claiming seven tankers hit overnight and then two more supertankers, and named data centres and cables in 7 Gulf states as targets. Mediation moved to Istanbul and to Munir's proposals in Tehran rather than Oman, and the US pulled nonessential staff from Saudi Arabia.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the former actor and comedian elected Ukraine's president in 2019, who has led the country through Russia's full-scale invasion.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant just after Trump's energy truce, and Seoul recalled its Kyiv envoy the same day. Since then Trump paused sanctions on Russia, Ukraine went 3 days without US missile warnings, Bessent rebuked Zelenskyy over Starlink, and Witkoff went from talks in Oslo to Moscow.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Nothing since the slide has pointed to a truce. Houthi strikes shut Riyadh's airport and led Qatar Airways to suspend flights to Riyadh and Dammam. A drone hit Shaybah, an attack on Dammam airport killed two, and British Typhoons began intercepting Houthi missiles. Saudi Arabia also postponed its investor summit to 2027.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport emptied the capital's skies and led Qatar Airways to suspend flights to Riyadh and Dammam. The war later reached Dammam, where a drone attack on the airport killed two, and drew in allies: British Typhoons now patrol Saudi skies, and Pakistan and Saudi Arabia ratified the Makkah defence pact with Turkey.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Trump and Putin moved closer through the month: their diesel deal sent the first 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel toward New York, and the Kremlin confirmed Abu Dhabi talks with the US in November, where Putin wants a final settlement on Ukraine. None of the news involved Xi.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the 2026 midterms. The House controls federal spending and can open investigations into the White House.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The one US election story of the fortnight was the charging of ex-FBI officials over their 2023 testimony, 11 days before the midterms. None of it bears on which party wins the House, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 2. Its price is what traders will stake on a deal that would reopen the Gulf's main oil export route.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Mediators multiplied: Lavrov offered Russia's services, Munir carried proposals to Tehran and seven foreign ministers met in Istanbul, yet Iran's security chief said no enriched uranium will leave. Meanwhile the Revolutionary Guard claimed mine strikes on tanker after tanker, and the US pulled nonessential staff from Saudi Arabia.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:MU.standing: An American maker of memory chips, DRAM and NAND flash, and one of three companies that make most of the world's DRAM. Its share price swings with the memory cycle and with demand for the high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers.
stocks:MU.recent: One of Micron's two Taiwan unions called a strike for Thursday in Taoyuan over bonuses. That dispute escalated after the shares had already fallen, and nothing reported about the company's own business accounts for the slide.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the war pausing this year.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.recent: Witkoff met Putin and the Kremlin confirmed US-brokered talks with Ukraine in Abu Dhabi in November, but Putin wants a final settlement, not a "short" truce. Melania Trump's ceasefire covers only occupied Oleshky, and Russia hit 28 energy facilities while Germany and Ukraine sought a full energy-sector truce.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google's own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of its Gemini 4 Argon, its only UK cloud region failed on a Tuesday morning and took banks and courts with it, and it softened its Gmail ad-targeting promise. None of the reporting ties any of these to the share's slide.
